messages:
maria (PM): quick intake: customer ACME is asking for per-customer quality thresholds + rollout controls. want to capture problem, goals, non-goals, success metrics, and a rough acceptance checklist so we can scope for Q3.

daniel (Eng): tl;dr on problem from CS? is this about routing fallback or model-level quality gating?

alexa (CS): ACME reported repeated regressions when we rolled quantized model v2 -> they want a hard gate: if output quality on their prompts drops >3% they want automatic rollback + alerting. They also want per-customer thresholds (different business lines = different tolerances).

maria (PM): Problem statement (draft): customers need per-customer quality SLAs during rollouts to avoid revenue-impacting regressions. Today we have org-wide evals & rollbacks; no per-customer gating. This blocks them from Dedicated and Private adoption.

sophie (Design): user-facing requirements: in Console we need a per-customer toggle, dropdown to pick evaluation set, and an override flow for manual review. low-fi mockup in Figma: link https://figma.com/s/xxxxx

ryan (SE): infra concerns: per-customer evals imply eval harness per customer + compute. do we evaluate live traffic (shadow) or run scheduled evals on stored prompt sets?

daniel (Eng): options: (A) shadow-traffic + online quality monitor (higher infra cost, low lag); (B) scheduled batch evals on customer prompt sets (cheaper, slower). also need a fallback policy: route to golden model or to Dedicated non-quantized pool.

maria (PM): Goals: 1) prevent regressions from reaching customers, 2) let customers set threshold and rollback policy, 3) surface clear metrics in Console + alerts to CS/SE. Non-goals: per-customer retraining, re-architecting serving routing, or long-term storage of all customers' prompt data (we'll assume customers provide small eval sets).

sophie (Design): success metrics: reduction in customer-visible regressions by 90% for pilot customers, <5% increase in average token cost for customers using gating, adoption by 3 pilot customers in first 8 weeks.

alexa (CS): acceptance criteria (proposal): - Customer can upload/select an eval set (<=500 prompts). - Console UI to set threshold % and rollback policy (auto/manual). - System runs scheduled evals pre-rollout and reports pass/fail. - On fail, model never promoted to production for that customer; if promoted earlier, automatic rollback + incident to CS.

daniel (Eng): edge cases: stale eval sets, small eval size (statistical significance), conflicting thresholds between org and customer, cross-customer model caching causing noisy signals. Need explicit handling in RFC.

ryan (SE): implementation notes: we can reuse Optimize's eval harness + tracing hooks. rough work items: 1) api for customer eval sets, 2) evaluate runner + result store, 3) rollout policy engine + per-customer routing flag, 4) Console controls + alerting integrations.

maria (PM): rough timeline: scoping spike (2w) -> MVP pilot (6w) -> iterate (4w). blockers: legal review for customer prompt storage, Dedicated routing complexity, and infra cost estimation.

oncall-bot: new-rfc created: /rfc/2026-07-per-customer-quality-gates.md (automated)

maria (PM): asks: @daniel can you own the spike and post a feasibility summary with cost ballpark? @ryan can you sketch required routing changes? @sophie can you add the console mockups to the PRD? @alexa can you confirm which pilot customers + get their eval sets? I'll draft PRD template sections and share by EOD tomorrow.

daniel (Eng): yep, picking up spike. will post notes by 1719900000 (~end of week). plan to include perf/cost sims for shadow vs batch eval.

ryan (SE): will sketch routing changes and highlight compatibility with Dedicated. will also call out KV cache impact.

sophie (Design): adding mockups and a short flow doc to the PRD.

alexa (CS): I'll ping ACME + two other pilots, ask for 300-500 exemplar prompts and the success definition per business line.

maria (PM): perfect. please keep replies short in this thread. we'll convert to RFC once spike is done. :thumbsup:
